label: Compute Pools & Cost Reporting
title:
Pick your clouds.
See what they cost.
subtitle: Build a compute pool from real, provider-native machines across seven clouds. Track token and compute usage per user, with budgets and quotas that keep spend predictable.
summary: Real multi-cloud machines with a placement strategy, plus per-user token and compute usage reporting.
highlights: Pools are built from each connected credential’s live catalog — concrete SKUs like cx33 or PRO2-S with real vCPU, RAM, disk, and price
Project, user, and installation scopes, resolved in that order
How agents are placed (Balanced, Pack, Spread, Smallest fit) and what happens when a provider is out of capacity (wait and retry, try other allowed machines, or stop with an error), per pool
Nodes are reused when they fit and stay warm for 30 minutes
Settings → Usage tracks token spend by model and day against a monthly budget; Admin → Costs and Admin → Usage cover the whole installation

screenshots.alt: Project compute pool editor with agents placed by Pack, Try other allowed machines when a provider is out of capacity, and a machine limit of 3 per person, above the allowed machines for each connection: Hetzner cx23 allowed in Falkenstein, cx33, cpx31 and cx43 with their regions and monthly prices, a sold-out Falkenstein region marked unavailable, and Scaleway machine types below
screenshots.caption: Choose exactly which machines SAM may rent, from every connected provider’s real catalog

details.headline: Real machines, not size labels
details.body: A compute pool lists the actual provider-native offerings it is allowed to rent — cx33, PRO2-S, vc2-4c-8gb, and more — across Hetzner, Scaleway, Vultr, Infomaniak, DigitalOcean, UpCloud, and GCP, each with its real vCPU, RAM, disk, and price. Every machine type a provider offers is listed with its regions: tap a region to let SAM start that machine there, or search by name or region. You choose how agents are placed (Balanced, Pack, Spread, Smallest fit) and what happens when a provider runs out of capacity (wait and retry, try other allowed machines, or stop with an error).

screenshot.alt: The allowed machines list: a search box, then Hetzner machine types with region buttons, cx23 allowed in Falkenstein, cx33 offered in Nuremberg, cpx31 in Helsinki, and cx43 whose Falkenstein region is sold out, followed by Scaleway machine types
screenshot.caption: Pick the regions where SAM may start each machine type, from every provider’s live catalog

details.headline: See why a node was chosen
details.body: Resource requirements resolve from task, trigger, skill, and agent profile down to project and platform defaults. The chat’s infrastructure panel shows the resolved requirement alongside the placement decision — which node won, and why.

screenshot.alt: Chat session details showing the requested vCPU, memory, and disk, the observed and configured hardware, the current compute pool with its strategy, and a saved placement decision explaining why a warm Hetzner node was reused
screenshot.caption: Every placement decision is explained, not just made

details.headline: One fleet, every provider
details.body: The Nodes page lists every machine across every connected provider side by side, with health, CPU/memory/disk usage, and price. Follow-up work reuses a warm node instead of waiting on a fresh boot.

screenshot.alt: Nodes page listing Hetzner, Scaleway, and Vultr machines side by side with status, health, observed and configured hardware, offering price, CPU, memory, and disk usage, and the workspaces on each
screenshot.caption: One fleet view across every connected cloud provider

details.headline: Token and compute usage, per user
details.body: Settings → Usage shows your AI usage by model and by day, against a monthly budget, for traffic routed through the SAM AI proxy. It also tracks your compute usage in node-hours against your quota. Admins get the installation-wide view — LLM spend by model, day, and user with a projection, plus per-user node usage — in Admin → Costs and Admin → Usage.

screenshot.alt: Settings → Usage page showing total cost, requests, and input and output tokens, a per-model breakdown, a daily cost trend, and budget controls with daily token limits and a monthly cost cap
screenshot.caption: Token usage by model and by day, against a monthly budget
